facts.fact: AP's coastline is about 974 km, the longest on India's east coast.
Arma Konda (~1,680 m) is the highest peak of AP and the Eastern Ghats.
The Godavari, the largest peninsular river, is the "Dakshina Ganga".
AP districts rose from 13 to 26 (4 April 2022) and to 28 with Polavaram and Markapuram.
AP's physiography: coastal plains, Eastern Ghats and the Rayalaseema plateau.
The Vamsadhara and Nagavali are shared with Odisha.
Polavaram on the Godavari is a National Project.
Nagarjuna Sagar and Srisailam are on the Krishna; Somasila on the Pennar.
AP has six agro-climatic zones; Kurnool–Anantapuramu form the Scarce Rainfall zone.
The AP coast is cyclone-prone; Rayalaseema (Anantapuramu) is semi-arid and drought-prone.
Deltaic alluvial soil characterises the Godavari–Krishna deltas.
Net area sown (~30.4%) is AP's largest land-use category.
ISFR 2023: AP forest cover ~18.46%; recorded forest area ~22.84%.
AP has India's second-largest mangroves; Coringa is the main sanctuary.
Nagarjunasagar–Srisailam is AP's tiger reserve.
Kolleru is AP's only Ramsar site.
Red Sanders (Pterocarpus santalinus) is endemic to AP's southern Eastern Ghats.
Jerdon's Courser, rediscovered in 1986, survives in Sri Lankamalleswara WLS.
Sri Venkateswara and Papikonda are AP national parks; Nelapattu is a pelican site.
Uranium occurs at Thummalapalli and black granite at Chimakurthy.
Southern tropical dry deciduous is AP's most widespread forest type.
Visakhapatnam is AP's only major port.
Handri-Neeva lifts Krishna water to Rayalaseema.
The Chenchu (PVTG) inhabit the Nallamala forests within NSTR.
AP comprises Coastal Andhra, Uttarandhra and Rayalaseema.
AP covers about 1.63 lakh km² and is India's 7th-largest state.
Monazite in AP beach sands is a source of thorium.
Srikakulam district has its headquarters at Srikakulam (Uttarandhra).
Parvathipuram Manyam district has its headquarters at Parvathipuram (Uttarandhra).
Vizianagaram district has its headquarters at Vizianagaram (Uttarandhra).
Visakhapatnam district has its headquarters at Visakhapatnam (Uttarandhra).
Alluri Sitharama Raju district has its headquarters at Paderu (Uttarandhra agency).
Anakapalli district has its headquarters at Anakapalli (Uttarandhra).
Kakinada district has its headquarters at Kakinada (Coastal Andhra).
East Godavari district has its headquarters at Rajamahendravaram (Coastal Andhra).
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema district has its headquarters at Amalapuram (Coastal Andhra).
Eluru district has its headquarters at Eluru (Coastal Andhra).
West Godavari district has its headquarters at Bhimavaram (Coastal Andhra).
NTR district has its headquarters at Vijayawada (Coastal Andhra).
Krishna district has its headquarters at Machilipatnam (Coastal Andhra).
Palnadu district has its headquarters at Narasaraopet (Coastal Andhra).
Guntur district has its headquarters at Guntur (Coastal Andhra).
Bapatla district has its headquarters at Bapatla (Coastal Andhra).
Prakasam district has its headquarters at Ongole (Coastal Andhra).
Sri Potti Sriramulu Nellore district has its headquarters at Nellore (Coastal Andhra (south)).
Kurnool district has its headquarters at Kurnool (Rayalaseema).
Nandyal district has its headquarters at Nandyal (Rayalaseema).
Anantapuramu district has its headquarters at Anantapur (Rayalaseema).
Sri Sathya Sai district has its headquarters at Puttaparthi (Rayalaseema).
YSR Kadapa district has its headquarters at Kadapa (Rayalaseema).
Annamayya district has its headquarters at Madanapalle (Rayalaseema).
Chittoor district has its headquarters at Chittoor (Rayalaseema).
Tirupati district has its headquarters at Tirupati (Rayalaseema/south coast).
Polavaram district has its headquarters at Rampachodavaram (Godavari agency).
Markapuram district has its headquarters at Markapuram (Prakasam west).
AP extends roughly from 12°41' N to 19°07' N and from 76°50' E to 84°45' E.
AP's area (about 1,62,970 km²) is about 4.96% of India.
Present-day (residuary) Andhra Pradesh came into being on 2 June 2014 after Telangana was carved out.
AP borders Odisha (north-east), Chhattisgarh (north), Telangana (north-west), Karnataka (west) and Tamil Nadu (south).
Before 2022 the 13 districts were 9 coastal and 4 Rayalaseema (Kurnool, Kadapa, Anantapur, Chittoor).
The 2022 reorganisation created 13 new districts, broadly one per Lok Sabha constituency.
Polavaram (HQ Rampachodavaram) and Markapuram districts came into force on 31 December 2025, taking AP to 28 districts.
Madanapalle is not a district; it is the headquarters town of Annamayya district.
The 28 zilla parishads for the new district map come into effect on 25 September 2026.
Arma Konda (Sitamma Konda/Jindhagada, about 1,680 m) in the Madugula Konda range, Alluri Sitharama Raju district, is the highest peak of AP and the Eastern Ghats.
The Ananthagiri hills (Araku valley) of Alluri Sitharama Raju district hold the Borra Caves and coffee estates.
The Papi Kondalu (Papikonda hills) form the Godavari gorge upstream of Polavaram.
The Kondapalli hills near Vijayawada (NTR district) are known for Kondapalli wooden toys (GI).
The Nallamala hills (Kurnool–Nandyal–Prakasam–Palnadu) between the Krishna and Penner hold Srisailam and NSTR.
The Erramala hills lie west of the Nallamala in Kurnool–Nandyal and hold the Belum Caves.
The Velikonda range runs along the Nellore–Prakasam border, east of the Nallamala.
The Palakonda hills are in YSR Kadapa district (red sanders belt).
The Lankamalla hills (Kadapa) shelter the Sri Lankamalleswara sanctuary of Jerdon's courser.
The Seshachalam hills (Tirupati–Kadapa) carry Tirumala and the Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve.
Horsley Hills (about 1,265 m, Annamayya district) is the "Ooty of Andhra".
Lambasingi (Chintapalli, Alluri Sitharama Raju) is called the "Kashmir of Andhra Pradesh" for its sub-zero winter nights.
Gandikota gorge on the Penner (YSR Kadapa) is called the "Grand Canyon of India".
Borra Caves (Ananthagiri hills, cut by the Gosthani) are limestone karst caves with stalactites, reported by William King in 1807.
Belum Caves (Kolimigundla, Nandyal) are the second-longest natural caves in the Indian subcontinent and the longest plains caves (about 3.2 km).
Yaganti (Nandyal) has Agastya and Venkateswara caves in the Erramala.
Rayalaseema is the south-eastern edge of the Deccan (Karnataka) plateau, about 300–600 m, with granite tors and Cuddapah sediments.
The crescent-shaped Cuddapah basin of Proterozoic sediments (quartzite, shale, limestone) underlies Kadapa–Kurnool and holds barytes, limestone and uranium.
The AP coastal plain is widest in the Godavari–Krishna delta and narrow in the north near Visakhapatnam.
The Eastern Ghats in AP average about 600 m and are broken by the Godavari and Krishna gaps.
Dolphin's Nose, a rocky headland, shelters the Visakhapatnam harbour; Kailasagiri hill overlooks the city.
Maredumilli in the Godavari agency is a forest eco-tourism area of the Eastern Ghats.
Below Dowleswaram (Rajamahendravaram) the Godavari splits into the Gautami (east) and Vasishta (west); Konaseema lies between them.
Yanam, an enclave of Puducherry, lies on the Gautami Godavari inside AP.
The Vasishta Godavari meets the sea at Antarvedi.
The Sabari (Kolab in Odisha) joins the Godavari near Kunavaram on the AP–Chhattisgarh–Telangana tri-junction.
The Sileru, upper Machkund, is a Sabari tributary with the Machkund, Upper Sileru and Lower Sileru (Donkarayi) hydel stations.
The Krishna enters the sea near Hamsaladeevi; its delta includes Diviseema island and Machilipatnam.
The Tungabhadra joins the Krishna near Sangameswaram (Nandyal/Kurnool), now inside the Srisailam reservoir.
The Munneru and Paleru are left-bank Krishna tributaries joining in NTR–Palnadu.
The Budameru, a stream near Vijayawada notorious for the 2024 floods, drains into Kolleru.
The Penna (Penner) flows through Anantapur, Kadapa and Nellore and enters the sea near Utukur/Nellore.
Penna tributaries: Jayamangali, Kunderu, Sagileru, Chitravathi, Papagni and Cheyyeru.
The Chitravathi rises in Karnataka and joins the Penna near Gandikota (Kadapa).
The Papagni rises in Karnataka and joins the Penna near Kamalapuram (Kadapa).
The Kunderu (Kundu) drains the Kurnool–Nandyal valley into the Penna.
The Vamsadhara rises in Kalahandi/Rayagada (Odisha) and reaches the sea at Kalingapatnam (Srikakulam).
The Nagavali (Langulya) rises in Kalahandi (Odisha) and reaches the sea near Srikakulam (Mofusbandar).
The Gundlakamma rises in the Nallamala and flows through Prakasam past Ongole.
The Swarnamukhi flows past Srikalahasti in Tirupati district.
The Gosthani rises in the Ananthagiri hills, carves the Borra Caves and reaches the sea at Bheemunipatnam.
The Yeleru (Kakinada) feeds the Yeleru reservoir supplying Visakhapatnam steel.
The Sarada and Varaha are short rivers of Anakapalli district.
AP has about 40 rivers, about 15 of them inter-state; all major rivers flow east to the Bay of Bengal.
Krishna waters were allocated by the Bachawat tribunal (KWDT-I, 1976) and KWDT-II (Brijesh Kumar); the Vamsadhara Water Disputes Tribunal (2010) settled the Neradi dispute with Odisha.
Sir Arthur Cotton built the Dowleswaram anicut on the Godavari (1852), rebuilt as the Sir Arthur Cotton Barrage.
The Prakasam Barrage at Vijayawada (1957) replaced Cotton's 1855 Krishna anicut.
Polavaram (Indira Sagar) multipurpose project on the Godavari was declared a national project under Section 90 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014.
The Pattiseema lift (2015–16) pumps Godavari water into the Polavaram right canal to the Krishna — the first Godavari–Krishna link.
Pulichintala reservoir on the Krishna lies on the Palnadu–Suryapet (Telangana) border.
The Telugu Ganga project (1983) carries Krishna water from Srisailam via the Kandaleru reservoir to Chennai.
Handri-Neeva Sujala Sravanthi lifts Krishna (Srisailam) flood water to Kurnool, Anantapur, Kadapa and Chittoor.
Galeru-Nagari Sujala Sravanthi carries Krishna water through the Gandikota reservoir to Kadapa–Chittoor.
The Veligonda (Pula Subbaiah) project tunnels through the Nallamala to take Srisailam water to western Prakasam (Markapuram).
The Kurnool–Cuddapah (KC) Canal (1860s) was built by the private Madras Irrigation Company on the Tungabhadra.
The Srisailam Right Branch Canal and Pothireddypadu head regulator divert Srisailam water to Rayalaseema.
Thotapalli barrage is on the Nagavali (Parvathipuram Manyam–Vizianagaram).
Gotta barrage (Hiramandalam) is on the Vamsadhara in Srikakulam.
The Machkund hydel project (1955) is a joint AP–Odisha project on the Machkund near Duduma falls.
Somasila (Penna) feeds the Kandaleru reservoir in Nellore district.
The Tungabhadra High Level and Low Level Canals irrigate Anantapur and Kurnool from the Tungabhadra dam.
Srisailam is mainly a hydel project with left- and right-bank power houses.
Kolleru Lake (Eluru–Krishna districts) became a Ramsar site in 2002 and a wildlife sanctuary in 1999.
Kolleru is fed by the Budameru and Tammileru and drains to the sea through the Upputeru.
Encroachment by aquaculture tanks led to "Operation Kolleru" (2006) to restore the lake to its +5 ft contour.
Pulicat lagoon (Tirupati district and Tamil Nadu) is a bird sanctuary famous for flamingos; the Flamingo Festival is held there.
Sriharikota island separates Pulicat lagoon from the Bay of Bengal and hosts the Satish Dhawan Space Centre.
Nelapattu Bird Sanctuary (Tirupati district) is a major breeding site of spot-billed pelicans.
Uppalapadu (Guntur) is a pelican and painted-stork bird sanctuary near Guntur city.
Telineelapuram and Telukunchi (Srikakulam) host migrant pelicans and painted storks.
Atapaka Bird Sanctuary is part of Kolleru (pelicans).
Kondakarla Ava (Anakapalli) is a large natural freshwater lake of north-coastal AP.
Hope Island, a sand spit built by Godavari sediment, shelters Kakinada Bay.
Re-measurement (2024) put India's coastline at 11,098.81 km and AP's at about 1,053 km — third after Gujarat and Tamil Nadu (traditional figure 974 km, longest on the east coast).
AP's coast runs from Ichchapuram (Srikakulam) in the north to Tada/Pulicat (Tirupati) in the south.
Gangavaram (near Visakhapatnam) is one of India's deepest ports (about 21 m draft).
Krishnapatnam is a deep-water port in Nellore district.
Ramayapatnam (Prakasam–Nellore), Machilipatnam and Mulapeta (Srikakulam) are new greenfield ports under construction.
Kakinada has an anchorage port and a deep-water port, and is a KG-basin gas hub.
The 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami struck the Krishna and Prakasam coasts (e.g., Nizampatnam).
AP has about 1,140 km² of coastal wetlands.
Anantapuramu is AP's driest district (about 550 mm rain) — often called India's second-driest after Jaisalmer.
The north-coastal agency (Srikakulam and Alluri Sitharama Raju) gets AP's highest rainfall.
Rentachintala (Palnadu) is often cited as the hottest place in AP.
The NE monsoon (Oct–Dec) is the main rain season for south-coastal AP (Nellore–Tirupati) and southern Rayalaseema.
Most of AP lies in seismic zones II and III; the coast and the Godavari–Krishna rift belt are Zone III.
The Godavari's record flood at Dowleswaram occurred in August 1986.
The November 1977 Diviseema cyclone (Krishna district) killed about 10,000 people through a huge storm surge.
The November 1996 Konaseema cyclone made landfall near Kakinada.
Cyclone Laila (May 2010) crossed the coast near Bapatla.
Cyclone Hudhud (October 2014, very severe) devastated Visakhapatnam.
Cyclone Titli (October 2018) struck Srikakulam near the Odisha border.
Cyclone Phethai (December 2018) crossed near Katrenikona (East Godavari/Konaseema).
Cyclone Gulab (September 2021) crossed near Kalingapatnam (Srikakulam).
Cyclone Michaung (5 December 2023) made landfall near Bapatla.
Severe Cyclone Montha made landfall near Narsapur on 28 October 2025, damaging about 87,000 ha of crops.
AP cyclones peak in the post-monsoon months (October–December), with a smaller May peak.
Mangampet (Kadapa region) holds one of the world's largest barytes deposits; AP is India's leading barytes producer.
Tummalapalle (YSR Kadapa) is among the world's largest uranium reserves, mined by UCIL.
Chimakurthy (Prakasam) is famous for "Black Galaxy" granite.
Limestone in Kadapa, Kurnool, Palnadu and Anantapur feeds a cement belt (Yerraguntla, Dachepalli).
Bauxite occurs in the Eastern Ghats agency of Alluri Sitharama Raju/Visakhapatnam (Araku, Chintapalli, Jerrela).
Heavy-mineral beach sands (ilmenite, rutile, garnet, monazite, zircon) occur from Srikakulam to Bheemunipatnam and Kakinada.
The Nellore–Gudur belt is AP's mica belt.
Diamonds occur in the Vajrakarur kimberlite pipes (Anantapur) and the historic Kollur gravels of the Krishna (source of the Koh-i-noor).
Gold occurs at Ramagiri (Sri Sathya Sai/Anantapur) and Chigargunta–Bisanatham (Chittoor).
Chrysotile asbestos occurs at Brahmanapalli near Pulivendula (YSR Kadapa).
Manganese ore occurs at Garbham (Vizianagaram) and in Srikakulam.
The Krishna–Godavari (KG) basin holds onshore and offshore oil and gas — Ravva field and the KG-D6 gas discovery (2002).
AP's mineral wealth earns it the name "Ratna Garbha".
Residuary AP has little coal (Chintalapudi, Eluru); the Godavari valley coalfield (Singareni) went to Telangana.
Dolomite and steatite are mined in the Kurnool–Kadapa (Cuddapah) belt.
AP forest types: southern tropical dry deciduous (dominant), moist deciduous (north-coastal agency), tropical thorn (Rayalaseema), tropical dry evergreen (south coast) and littoral/mangrove forests.
Red sanders grows in the Seshachalam, Lankamalla, Palakonda and Veligonda hills of Kadapa, Tirupati, Chittoor, Annamayya, Nellore and Kurnool.
Alluri Sitharama Raju has the largest forest cover among AP districts (ISFR 2023).
Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary (1978, Kakinada) protects Godavari-estuary mangroves.
Krishna Wildlife Sanctuary (1989) protects the Krishna-estuary mangroves (Krishna–Bapatla).
Rollapadu (Nandyal/Kurnool) protects the great Indian bustard and lesser florican.
Sri Lankamalleswara WLS (YSR Kadapa) is the only home of Jerdon's courser.
Koundinya WLS (Chittoor) is AP's elephant sanctuary, part of the Rayala Elephant Reserve.
Gundla Brahmeswaram WLS lies in the Nallamala (Nandyal–Prakasam), adjoining NSTR.
Sri Penusila Narasimha WLS is in Nellore district (Velikonda hills).
Kambalakonda WLS lies in Visakhapatnam city's hills.
NSTR was declared a tiger reserve in 1983 and spreads over Nandyal, Prakasam, Palnadu, Kurnool and Guntur; its Telangana part became Amrabad TR.
Rajiv Gandhi (Rameswaram) NP in YSR Kadapa is AP's smallest national park.
Indira Gandhi Zoological Park (Visakhapatnam) and Sri Venkateswara Zoological Park (Tirupati) are AP's big zoos.
AP's state animal is the blackbuck (Krishna Jinka).
AP's state bird is the rose-ringed parakeet (Rama Chiluka), adopted in 2018.
AP's state tree is the neem (Vepa).
AP's state flower is jasmine (Malle).
The golden gecko of the Tirumala–Seshachalam hills is an endemic reptile of AP.
Olive ridley turtles nest on the AP coast (e.g., Srikakulam, Kakinada, Krishna).
Talakona (Sri Venkateswara NP, Tirupati district) is AP's highest waterfall (about 82 m).
Ethipothala falls on the Chandravanka stream lies near Nagarjuna Sagar (Palnadu) with a crocodile breeding centre.
Katiki falls on the Gosthani lies near the Borra Caves (Alluri Sitharama Raju).
Kailasakona falls lies near Puttur/Nagari (Tirupati–Chittoor).
Ubbalamadugu (Tada) falls lies in Tirupati district near Varadaiahpalem.
Rampa falls lies near Rampachodavaram (Polavaram district).
Duduma falls on the Machkund forms the AP–Odisha border.
The Srisailam reservoir is named Neelam Sanjiva Reddy Sagar.
The Nagarjuna Sagar right canal (Jawahar canal) irrigates Palnadu, Guntur and Prakasam; the left canal (Lal Bahadur Shastri canal) Telangana and NTR–Krishna.
Pulichintala reservoir is named K.L. Rao Sagar.
Velugodu (Nandyal) and Brahmamgari Matham (Kadapa) are Telugu Ganga balancing reservoirs.
Mylavaram and Gandikota reservoirs are on the Penna in Kadapa.
The Chitravathi Balancing Reservoir lies in Anantapur–Sri Sathya Sai.
Raiwada (Sarada) and Thandava reservoirs serve Anakapalli.
Madduvalasa reservoir (Suvarnamukhi, Vizianagaram) is a north-coastal project.
The North Coastal zone covers Srikakulam, Vizianagaram and Visakhapatnam plains.
The Godavari zone covers the East and West Godavari delta and uplands.
The Krishna zone covers Krishna, Guntur and parts of Prakasam (black soils, cotton, chillies).
The Southern zone covers Nellore, Chittoor and parts of Kadapa, with NE-monsoon rain.
The Scarce Rainfall zone covers Kurnool and Anantapur (plus parts of Kadapa and Prakasam), growing groundnut and millets.
The High Altitude & Tribal Areas zone covers the Eastern Ghats agency (coffee, pepper, millets).
Red soils (sandy and loamy) cover the largest share of AP, followed by black soils; alluvial soils line the deltas.
Black soils dominate Krishna–Guntur–Prakasam and western Kurnool–Nandyal, growing cotton, chillies and tobacco.
The Godavari–Krishna delta is called the "Rice Bowl" of AP; Konaseema is noted for coconut.
Coastal sandy and saline soils fringe the shore, with problem saline patches in Nellore and Krishna.
